record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.original_question: Improve the theoretical determination of higher-order QCD contributions to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment (g−2)μ. The open question is how to reduce the Standard Model uncertainty from QCD effects so that future higher-precision muon magnetic-moment measurements can more sharply test the Standard Model and possible extensions of it.

evidence.quote: At present the precision of the theoretical estimate of (gµ − 2) is principally limited by the lack of information on higher order QCD contributions, which require further study.
Approved experiments at BNL plan to reduce the statistical and systematic uncertainties on aµ to about 0.3 ppm, making better understanding of the QCD contribution a very high priority.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a_\mu = (g_\mu - 2)/2$ denote the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, defined via the Dirac form factor decomposition of the muon's electromagnetic vertex at zero momentum transfer. Within the Standard Model, $a_\mu$ admits a decomposition
$$a_\mu^{\mathrm{SM}} = a_\mu^{\mathrm{QED}} + a_\mu^{\mathrm{EW}} + a_\mu^{\mathrm{HVP}} + a_\mu^{\mathrm{HLbL}},$$
where $a_\mu^{\mathrm{HVP}}$ is the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution (starting at order $\alpha^2$) and $a_\mu^{\mathrm{HLbL}}$ is the hadronic light-by-light contribution (starting at order $\alpha^3$). These hadronic pieces dominate the total theoretical uncertainty on $a_\mu^{\mathrm{SM}}$.

Problem: Develop a theoretical determination of the higher-order QCD (hadronic) contributions $a_\mu^{\mathrm{HVP}}$ and $a_\mu^{\mathrm{HLbL}}$ — for example via dispersive analyses based on $e^+e^- \to \mathrm{hadrons}$ data, lattice QCD, or effective field theory techniques — that reduces the total Standard Model theoretical uncertainty on $a_\mu$ to a level commensurate with sub-ppm experimental precision, so that a meaningful comparison between $a_\mu^{\mathrm{SM}}$ and the measured value $a_\mu^{\mathrm{exp}}$ can be used to test the Standard Model and constrain possible extensions. Quantify and control all sources of uncertainty in the hadronic contributions.
artifact.category_tag: Hadronic contributions to muon anomalous magnetic moment
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2025/2026, substantial progress has been made on the hadronic contributions via lattice QCD and dispersive methods. The Muon g-2 Theory Initiative released an updated White Paper in 2025 with prediction $a_\mu = (116592033 \pm 62) \times 10^{-11}$ (530 ppb), now consistent with the Fermilab experimental result at 127 ppb. However, tensions remain between different evaluations of the HVP contribution (e.g., between lattice QCD and earlier $e^+e^-$ data-driven results, and among $e^+e^-$ datasets), and the hadronic pieces still dominate the theory error. The problem is therefore actively progressing but not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: White Paper (2025) - Muon g-2 Theory Initiative
status_evidence.snippet: Updated Standard Model prediction with uncertainty of 530 ppb, dominated by hadronic contributions.
status_evidence.claim: Hadronic contributions remain the dominant theoretical uncertainty; an updated SM prediction was released in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Fermilab's final word on muon g-2 – CERN Courier
status_evidence.snippet: Final Fermilab result at 127 ppb; tensions reside in theoretical hadronic determinations.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental precision now far exceeds 0.3 ppm; theory uncertainty is the limiting factor and is being actively reduced.

status_evidence.title: Muon g-2 achieves record precision, but theoretical tensions remain
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical tensions in hadronic contributions persist between lattice QCD and data-driven approaches.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is partially solved: significant progress but unresolved tensions remain.
